content: DEFB103A, also known as Beta-defensin 103, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the DEFB103A gene. Defensins are a family of peptides that exhibit both microbicidal and cytotoxic properties, and they are primarily produced by neutrophils. Members of the defensin family share a high degree of similarity in their protein sequences. The DEFB103A gene encodes the protein defensin beta 103B, which demonstrates broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. This protein is believed to play a critical role in the innate immune defense of epithelial tissues, providing a protective barrier against microbial invasion. In dogs, the product of the corresponding genetic locus, β-Defensin 103, has an additional function beyond its antimicrobial role. It acts as an agonist of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), contributing to the regulation of pigmentation.
